_comment: Every external endpoint used by the MARSWALK data pipeline.
Each entry was opened and verified on 2026-11-13; 'verified' records what
the probe actually returned. Nothing in this file is a guessed URL.
provenance: REAL = downloaded from NASA/USGS; DERIVED = computed by us from
REAL data; MODELED = built from published measurements, not a raw dataset.
AOI = footprint of the HiRISE DTM that covers Curiosity's traverse from
the Glen Torridon clay-bearing unit (sol ~1167) through Gediz Vallis to
the sulfate-bearing unit and the 2025 boxwork campaign (sol 5070).
This is NOT the 5.4S/137.8E point in the original brief: no HiRISE DTM
covers that point, and Curiosity has never been there. See README.

dem.title: MRO HiRISE Digital Terrain Model, Gale Crater filled channel and fan deposit
dem.access: HTTP range requests (server sends Accept-Ranges: bytes), so only the AOI rows are downloaded, not the full ~540 MB file
dem.verified: 2026-11-13: HEAD 200, Accept-Ranges bytes; label parsed; sample row returned continuous float elevations

ortho.title: MRO HiRISE, Curiosity Roving Site Mosaic
ortho.tile_scheme: geographic, top-left (-180, 90), matrix 2^(z+1) x 2^z, 256 px tiles
ortho.verified: 2026-11-13: WMTSCapabilities parsed; tiles return 8-bit greyscale PNG

traverse.title: Curiosity actual driven path
traverse.fields: RMC, site, drive, sol, easting, northing, elev_geoid, lon, lat, roll, pitch, yaw, tilt

geology.title: Global Geologic Map of Mars (USGS SIM 3292)
geology.source: USGS Astrogeology, served via NASA Mars Trek
geology.verified: 2026-11-13: present in the Trek catalog as a global product

science_regions.product_name: Curiosity's Proposed Path up Mount Sharp
science_regions.note: Annotated regions (clay-bearing unit, Greenheugh pediment, Gediz Vallis ridge, Gediz Vallis channel, sulfate-bearing unit) digitized as GeoJSON and georeferenced to the DTM. Labelled 'digitized from NASA/JPL-Caltech annotated map' in the UI.

radiation.citation: Hassler, D. M. et al. (2014), Mars' Surface Radiation Environment Measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity Rover, Science 343, 1244797
radiation.note: Baseline surface dose rate and the solar-particle-event scenario are modelled from published RAD results, not ingested telemetry. The SPE is explicitly labelled a scenario in the UI.

weather.basis: Curiosity REMS published seasonal values for Gale Crater
weather.note: Daily temperature, pressure and wind cycle modelled from published REMS ranges; dust opacity is a user-selectable scenario, not a measurement.

rejected._comment: Sources checked and NOT used, with the reason. Kept so the choice is auditable.

trek_gale_dem_tiles.reason: Trek serves this DEM as 8-bit greyscale PNG tiles: a whole z=14 tile contains only ~5 distinct grey levels, i.e. roughly 14 m of elevation per level once stretched over Gale's relief. Adequate as a picture, unusable for slope or hazard derivation. Replaced by the 32-bit float PDS DTM.

usgs_mola_463m.reason: Real and reachable (2.1 GB GeoTIFF) but 463 m/px gives ~15 x 32 pixels over this AOI. Too coarse for EVA routing.

usgs_hrsc_mola_blend_200m.reason: 404 - the filename guessed from memory does not exist. Not used.

murray_lab_ctx.reason: Host unreachable from the build environment at probe time.

nasa_worldview.reason: Earth observation data. Used only as design inspiration for the layer UX, credited on the About page. No Earth data is placed on the Mars map.

perseverance_raw_images.reason: Mars 2020 operates in Jezero Crater, not Gale. Listed on the About page as a related resource only.
